financials_interim.notes: E M L Consultants PLC (EML), engineering/project consultancy, single-entity company (no subsidiaries; no Group/Company split in this filing), FYE 31 December. GROUP basis used per convention for single-entity filer. Source PDF is a scanned/OCR'd document with heavily garbled machine-readable text; all figures below were cross-checked against the filing's own clean rendered tables (page 3 income statement, page 4 balance sheet, page 6 cash flow, page 3 statement of changes in equity) and verified via accounting identities -- see checks below -- not taken from the garbled OCR layer. Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026, column '01.04.2026 to 30.06.2026') vs Q2 2025 (quarter ended 30 June 2025, column '01.04.2025 to 30.06.2025') -- both explicitly presented on the face P&L, a genuine same-quarter YoY compare (the filing also gives six-month YTD columns, not used for the quarterly fields below). cost_of_sales = 'Direct Cost' (-12,010,201); gross_profit = 4,145,296 (=Revenue-Direct Cost, ties). operating_profit = 'Operating Profit/(Loss)' = 623,296 (Gross profit + Other Income - Administrative Expenses = 4,145,296+8,543,641-12,065,641=623,296, ties). finance_income = 1,519,536, the filing's own net 'Finance Income - net' line (labelled as net, no separate finance_costs split disclosed, so finance_costs left blank -- not a data omission, the filing genuinely presents this as a single net line). tax_expense=0 -- 'Income Tax' line is a dash/nil in BOTH the current and comparative quarter (consistent with the company reporting losses/thin profits recently, plausibly using brought-forward tax losses, though the filing gives no note explaining the nil tax charge -- genuine disclosure gap, not assumed by us). profit_after_tax = profit_before_tax exactly (2,142,832) since tax=0. eps_basic=eps_diluted=0.02 -- only one EPS line disclosed ('Basic Earnings/(Loss) per Share'); cross-check: 2,142,832 / 90,900,000 shares = 0.0236, rounds to 0.02, ties. shares_in_issue=90,900,000 per Note 6.3 'Total No of Shares As at 30 June 2026'. No segmental note is presented anywhere in this filing (notes 1-6 cover basis of preparation, accounting policy continuity, contingent liabilities [an EPF/ETF labour tribunal case, Case No 27/Anu/2546/2020, partly heard, no provision quantified as outcome uncertain], subsequent events, and share information only) -- EML does not disclose a business-line/segment breakdown, a genuine information gap given this is a diversified consultancy; growth attribution below is therefore limited to the P&L line items actually shown (Revenue, Direct Cost, Other Income, Administrative Expenses). short_term_borrowings=6,539,625 = 'Loans and Borrowings' (current) -- per the cash flow note's cash & cash equivalents breakdown (page 6), this figure exactly equals the 'Total Unfavourable Cash & Cash Equivalent' balance (Local Current Accounts, i.e. a bank overdraft position), so this is functionally an overdraft, not a term loan -- flagged, not re-labelled. long_term_borrowings=0 -- 'Loans and Borrowings' non-current line is blank/nil at both 30 June 2026 and 31 Dec 2025. inventory left blank -- no inventory line exists on this consultancy's balance sheet (professional services, no goods held for sale); 'Consultation Work-In-Progress' (a services-in-progress asset, nil at 30 June 2026, Rs.5,389,763 at 31 Dec 2025) is NOT populated into the inventory field as it is conceptually distinct (unbilled service costs, not goods inventory) and is a period-end balance sheet item outside the standard field set requested. capex left blank -- the investing-activities section of the cash flow statement (page 6) discloses only 'Interest received' and '(Investment)/uplift in short term investment', with NO purchase-of-PP&E line at all, despite PP&E rising Rs.172,787 net of the period's Rs.1,166,376 depreciation charge on the balance sheet (implying an implied, undisclosed capex/transfer of roughly Rs.1.34mn) -- a genuine gap in this filing's cash flow disclosure, not an omission on our part. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: cash_from_operations/cash_from_investing/cash_from_financing are the filing's 6-MONTHS ended 30 June 2026 CUMULATIVE figures (7,285,907 / -2,213,930 / -5,236,267), NOT quarterly -- EML's cash flow statement is only presented on a 6-month YTD basis, no quarterly-only breakout given (same limitation as CTC this batch). Identity checks, all tie exactly: Revenue-Direct Cost=Gross Profit (16,155,497-12,010,201=4,145,296); Gross Profit+Other Income-Admin Expenses=Operating Profit (4,145,296+8,543,641-12,065,641=623,296); Operating Profit+Finance Income=PBT (623,296+1,519,536=2,142,832); PBT-0 tax=PAT (2,142,832); PAT ties to the Statement of Changes in Equity's 'Total Comprehensive Income For The Period' six-month figure of 2,313,465 when H1 2026 PBT (2,313,465) - 0 tax is used instead (6-month figures, separately verified, both non-quarterly rows tie to equity roll-forward exactly); total_liabilities (66,159,887) + total_equity (199,818,520) = 265,978,407 = total_assets, ties exactly at 30 June 2026.

thesis.thesis_text: E M L Consultants PLC is a small engineering/project consultancy that swung to a Rs.2,142,832 profit in Q2 2026 from a Rs.4,780,723 loss a year earlier, but the swing was driven almost entirely by a Rs.6,075,187 (+246% YoY) jump in an unexplained 'Other Income' line rather than core operations -- gross margin actually compressed to 25.7% from 33.6% as costs grew faster than the 76.7% revenue increase. Derived Q1 2026 revenue fell 14.9% YoY, suggesting this quarter's growth is not representative of the business's underlying, lumpy project-based revenue pattern. At Rs.8.10, the stock trades on a run-rate P/E over 100x and P/B of ~3.69x -- expensive for a business whose core operating profit was only Rs.623,296 this quarter (Q2 2026 interim, source_doc_id 52529).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/construction-sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). This is EML's first and only interim financial_statements entry -- no prior quarter for QoQ comparison, no annual report reviewed, and no dividend history exists. The source filing is a scanned/OCR'd document with a garbled machine-readable text layer; figures used were cross-checked against the filing's clean rendered tables and accounting identities, per financial_statements notes, but this adds an extra layer of uncertainty. The P/E cited is a rough run-rate approximation and is unusually sensitive to the unexplained Other Income swing driving this quarter's profit.

financial_quality.rationale: Q2 2026 Group PAT of Rs.2,142,832 swung from a Rs.4,780,723 loss a year earlier, but the swing was driven overwhelmingly by a Rs.6,075,187 (+246%) jump in an unexplained 'Other Income' line -- larger than the entire Rs.1,074,092 increase in Gross Profit almost six-fold -- rather than core operations; gross margin actually compressed to 25.7% from 33.6% as Direct Cost (+97.7%) outpaced Revenue (+76.7%). Run-rate ROE is low at ~4.3% (annualized PAT ~Rs.8.57mn / total equity Rs.199.82mn). Leverage is minimal (short-term borrowings only Rs.6.54mn, effectively an overdraft; no long-term debt), but that reflects a small, thinly-profitable balance sheet more than financial strength.

growth_outlook.rationale: Q2 2026 Revenue grew 76.7% YoY to Rs.16,155,497, but this was not representative of the underlying trend: derived Q1 2026 revenue (H1 minus Q2) actually fell 14.9% YoY, consistent with lumpy, project-based consultancy revenue recognition. H1 2026 PAT of Rs.2,313,465 was far smaller than the standalone Q2 swing would suggest. No segmental or service-line breakdown is disclosed to identify which part of the business is actually growing.

valuation.rationale: At price Rs.8.10 (as of 2026-08-28), run-rate annualized EPS of ~Rs.0.08 (quarterly EPS 0.02 x4, a rough approximation given how volatile and Other-Income-dependent this quarter's profit was) implies a P/E of over 100x. Market cap of Rs.736.29mn against total equity of Rs.199.82mn implies a P/B of ~3.69x. Both multiples are expensive for a company whose core operating profit was only Rs.623,296 this quarter and whose swing to profitability depended on an unexplained income line; no dividend is on record.

business_quality.rationale: EML is a small engineering/project consultancy with no disclosed segmental or business-line breakdown, meaning growth and profitability cannot be attributed to specific service lines -- a genuine information gap for a diversified consultancy. Revenue recognition is evidently lumpy and project-driven (Q1 2026 revenue fell 14.9% YoY even as Q2 grew 76.7%), which limits earnings predictability and moat assessment.

governance_risk.rationale: An EPF/ETF-related labour tribunal case (Case No 27/Anu/2546/2020) remains partly heard with no provision quantified in the filing -- an unresolved contingent liability. No income tax was charged in either period with no explanatory note, and the dominant driver of this quarter's profit swing (Other Income, +Rs.6,075,187) is not broken down anywhere in the filing -- both genuine disclosure-quality concerns.

interim_updates.note_text: E M L Consultants PLC (EML) swung to a Profit After Tax of Rs.2,142,832 for Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) from a Loss of Rs.4,780,723 in Q2 2025, a turnaround of Rs.6,923,555. Revenue grew 76.7% YoY to Rs.16,155,497 (2025: Rs.9,145,292), while Direct Cost rose even faster, +97.7% to Rs.12,010,201 (2025: Rs.6,074,088), so Gross Profit grew a more modest 35.0% to Rs.4,145,296 (2025: Rs.3,071,204) -- gross margin actually compressed to 25.7% from 33.6% even as absolute gross profit rose. The dominant driver of the swing to profitability, however, was Other Income, which surged 246.1% YoY to Rs.8,543,641 (2025: Rs.2,468,454), a Rs.6,075,187 increase that on its own exceeds the entire Rs.1,074,092 increase in Gross Profit nearly six-fold; the filing does not break down what comprises Other Income, so the source of this swing cannot be further attributed. Administrative Expenses were essentially flat, +0.4% YoY to Rs.12,065,641 (2025: Rs.12,015,971), so they were neither a driver nor a drag. Operating Profit swung to Rs.623,296 from an Operating Loss of Rs.6,476,313. Finance Income (net) fell 10.4% YoY to Rs.1,519,536 (2025: Rs.1,695,590), a modest headwind. No income tax was charged in either period (nil both years), so Profit Before Tax (Rs.2,142,832 vs a loss of Rs.4,780,723) flowed straight through to Profit After Tax. Basic EPS improved to Rs.0.02 from a loss per share of Rs.(0.05). For the six months ended 30 June 2026, PAT was a much smaller Rs.2,313,465 (2025: a loss of Rs.5,924,531) -- since H1 revenue grew only 8.1% YoY (Rs.39,385,050 vs Rs.36,428,857) versus Q2 alone growing 76.7%, this implies Q1 2026 revenue (calculated as H1 minus Q2: Rs.23,229,553) actually FELL 14.9% YoY versus Q1 2025 (calculated: Rs.27,283,565) -- so the quarter's growth was not representative of the first half as a whole, consistent with lumpy, project-based revenue recognition typical of a consultancy. No segmental or business-line breakdown is disclosed anywhere in this filing, so growth cannot be attributed to specific service lines or projects beyond the P&L line items shown.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for EML -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No segmental/business-line note is disclosed anywhere in this filing (notes cover only basis of preparation, accounting policy continuity, contingent liabilities, subsequent events and share information) -- a genuine information gap, not a data-entry omission, so growth cannot be attributed to specific service lines. The composition of 'Other Income' (the dominant YoY driver, +Rs.6,075,187) is not broken down anywhere in the filing. The investing section of the cash flow statement discloses no purchase-of-PP&E/capex line at all despite a small net increase in PP&E on the balance sheet -- capex is therefore left blank rather than estimated. Cash flow figures stored in financial_statements are 6-month cumulative (the only basis disclosed), not quarterly -- flagged in that row's notes field; this does not affect the YoY figures here, which are all drawn from the reliable 3-month P&L columns. finance_costs is not split from finance_income (only a net 'Finance Income - net' line is given). The source PDF is a scanned/OCR'd document with a garbled machine-readable text layer; all figures used here were taken from the filing's own clean rendered tables and cross-verified via accounting identities (documented in the financial_statements row's notes field), not from the raw OCR text.
interim_updates.takeaway: EML's swing from a Rs.4,780,723 loss to a Rs.2,142,832 profit in Q2 2026 was driven overwhelmingly by a 246.1% (Rs.6,075,187) jump in Other Income rather than core operating performance -- Direct Cost actually grew faster than Revenue, compressing gross margin from 33.6% to 25.7%. Because Other Income is not broken down in the filing, the durability of this driver cannot be assessed from the document alone. Investors should also note that Q2's 76.7% revenue growth is not representative of the first half: derived Q1 2026 revenue actually fell 14.9% YoY, consistent with lumpy, project-based revenue recognition typical of a consultancy, and H1 2026 PAT of Rs.2,313,465 is much smaller than the standalone Q2 profit would suggest.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.16,155,497, +76.7% YoY (2025: Rs.9,145,292); Operating Profit Rs.623,296 vs an Operating Loss of Rs.6,476,313 a year earlier; PAT Rs.2,142,832 vs a Loss of Rs.4,780,723 a year earlier.

Other Income surged 246.1% YoY to Rs.8,543,641 (2025: Rs.2,468,454), a Rs.6,075,187 increase -- the single largest driver of the swing to profitability, exceeding the Rs.1,074,092 rise in Gross Profit nearly six-fold. No breakdown of Other Income is disclosed.
Gross margin compressed to 25.7% (2025: 33.6%) even as absolute Gross Profit rose 35.0%, because Direct Cost (+97.7% YoY) grew faster than Revenue (+76.7% YoY).
Administrative Expenses essentially flat YoY (+0.4%, Rs.12,065,641 vs Rs.12,015,971).
No income tax charged in either period (nil both years) -- no explanatory note given.

Derived: Q1 2026 revenue (H1 minus Q2, Rs.23,229,553) fell 14.9% YoY vs Q1 2025 (Rs.27,283,565), even though Q2 2026 revenue grew 76.7% YoY -- growth this quarter is not representative of H1 2026 as a whole (H1 PAT of Rs.2,313,465 vs an H1 2025 loss of Rs.5,924,531).
Contingent liability: an EPF/ETF-related labour tribunal case (Case No 27/Anu/2546/2020) remains partly heard with hearing dates not yet fixed; no provision is quantified in the filing.
key_drivers: Other Income +246.1% YoY (Rs.8,543,641 vs Rs.2,468,454, a Rs.6,075,187 increase) -- the dominant, quantified driver of the swing from an operating loss to an operating profit; not broken down further by the filing.

Direct Cost grew faster than Revenue (+97.7% vs +76.7% YoY), compressing gross margin from 33.6% to 25.7% -- a genuine cost-side headwind that would have limited the swing to profit had Other Income not offset it.
No income tax charge in either period meant the full Rs.6,923,555 PBT swing flowed straight to PAT, with no tax-related drag or benefit (unlike some peers this quarter).
